clippings.speaker: Saul Bass
clippings.quote: I happened to be working on the symbols for Otto Preminger’s Carmen Jones and The Man With The Golden Arm and at some point, Otto and I just looked at each other and said, “Why not make it move?” It was as simple as that.
clippings.film: The Man with the Golden Arm
clippings.title: Saul Bass on his approach to designing movie title sequences
clippings.context: Excerpt from a 1977 interview of Bass by Herbert Yager, reproduced by Jason Kottke; Bass on how his moving title sequences began with Preminger.

clippings.speaker: Saul Bass
clippings.quote: [w]hen Otto learned that his The Man with the Golden Arm was opening over closed drapes he made sure that there was a note attached to every print instructing the projectionist not to run the first reel until the curtains had been drawn back.
clippings.film: The Man with the Golden Arm
clippings.title: From Saul Bass to participatory culture: Opening title sequences in contemporary television series
clippings.context: Valentina Re quotes Bass's recollection as cited from Pat Kirkham (1994, p. 16), on Preminger protecting the 1955 title sequence.

notes: Very thin: no fetchable Preminger quote about Bass found (Ebert's 'Ottobiography' interview with a Bass anecdote and the Medium copy of the Yager interview both returned 403; Haskin's Film Quarterly interview is JSTOR-only). The 'jumped off the roof for Otto' line appears only on IMDb, unsourced, so it was skipped.
